To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-17A signaling promotes colon tumorigenicity through the IL-17RA-IL-17RC heterodimer and that IL-17 signaling is required to sustain LGR5-positive colon stem cells.
IL-17 signaling promotes the development of colitis-associated colorectal cancer by inducing proliferation of LGR5-positive colon epithelial cells through activation of ERK and JNK MAPKs.
IL-17A promotes colon tumorigenic potential by signaling through the IL-17RA/IL-17RC heterodimeric complex to activate the ERK5-ERK1/2 cascade in LGR5-expressing stem cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IL-17 signaling in the development of colon tumorigenisis.
the role of IL-17 in colon epithelium maintenance and tumorigenisis.
understanding the mechanisms of IL-17R signaling in colon epithelial cell homeostasis and cancer development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-17A signaling in LGR5 positive stem cells promotes colon epithelium regeneration after injury, and contributes to colon tumorigenicity.
IL-17 signaling through IL-17RC-Act1- TRAF4 cascade promotes colon homeostasis and regeneration by activating MAPK signaling in the LGR 5-positive stem cells.
IL-17 signaling in LGR5+ cells promotes colon tumorgenesis by activating MAPKs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IL-17/Act1/TRAF4/MAPK cascade in LGR5+ stem cells promotes the regeneration of colon epithelium and the development of colitis-associated tumors by sustaining stem cells with a genetic lesion.
the IL-17A-Act1-ERK cascade promotes colon epithelium regeneration after injury, contributing to colon tumour development.
IL-17A promotes colon cancer through a stem cell niche.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IL-17 signaling axis plays an important role in the development of colitis-associated colorectal cancer.
IL-17A signaling in colon epithelium promotes tumorigenesis in the context of chronic inflammation.
the IL-17 signaling axis plays an important role in colon epithelium regeneration after injury and that this pathway is a therapeutic target for colon tumorigenensis.
